_comment: Feasibility study cards (src/sim/studies.ts, EDUCATION D14). trlNow is a real-world estimate (claim FS-1, UNVERIFIED); humanYears, sigma, costBUSD and pSuccess are game knobs. effects reuse the program effect kinds (src/sim/programs.ts). requires: study ids that must have succeeded first. group: competing lines shown together (parallel funding).

studies.name: HIVE SURVEY 1: VISIBLE CUBESAT SWARM
breakthroughs: onboard detection so nodes send cut-outs, not raw frames
laser links between small spacecraft at a useful rate
studies.note: Sixteen small telescopes near the Earth's orbit stacked as one: sixteen 15 cm mirrors collect as much light as one 60 cm mirror.

studies.name: HIVE SURVEY 2: 64 NODES ABOVE AND BELOW THE PLANE
breakthroughs: shift-and-add search over many trial motions at scale
spacecraft spread far enough apart to see parallax on the first night
studies.note: Sixty-four nodes collect like one 1.2 m mirror; spread out, they see a new rock from several angles and know its distance at once (tighter orbits).

studies.name: HIVE SURVEY 3: INFRARED NODES WITH VENUS AND L4/L5 LEGS
breakthroughs: keeping an infrared detector cold on a small spacecraft
navigating and linking a swarm across the inner solar system
studies.note: Infrared sees heat, so dark rocks show up too; legs inside the Earth's orbit look outward with the Sun behind them.

studies.name: FISSION POWER 40 KWE (HEAT PIPES)
breakthroughs: a flight-qualified reactor and converter
launch safety approval
studies.note: A small reactor with no pumps: heat pipes carry the heat to engines that make electricity. The first step to power far from the Sun.

studies.name: FISSION POWER 1 MWE (LIQUID-LITHIUM LOOP)
breakthroughs: pumped liquid-metal loops that run for years
radiators that reject a megawatt hot
studies.note: Enough power for electric propulsion on every interceptor (a little more launch energy in the game). Every watt ends as heat that must be radiated away.

studies.name: LIQUID DROPLET RADIATOR
breakthroughs: spraying hot droplets across open space and catching all of them again
studies.note: A sheet of hot droplets radiates like a huge panel but weighs far less. Radiated power goes as temperature to the fourth power: hot radiators are small radiators.

studies.name: ORBITAL COMPUTE MOTHERSHIP (300 KW)
breakthroughs: computers that survive radiation for years
rejecting hundreds of kilowatts of cool waste heat
studies.note: The brain of the swarm: fits orbits, points the telescopes and writes the reports. Better tracking in the game.

studies.name: LATTICE CONFINEMENT FUSION (BEAM-TRIGGERED)
breakthroughs: more fusion energy out than the beam puts in
an open question: can a compact X-ray source trigger it, as the original experiments did with gamma rays?
studies.note: Deuterium packed into a metal lattice; a beam makes fast deuterons that fuse at short range. Fusion products have been seen in the lab; net energy has not.

studies.name: FIELD-REVERSED CONFIGURATION (SPACE POWER AND THRUST)
breakthroughs: a plasma ring that holds long enough to burn
turning fusion output straight into thrust
studies.note: A self-organised plasma ring in a straight machine: the best magnetic candidate for a fusion rocket. Success gives REALISTIC runs a weaker fusion tug.

studies.name: SHEARED-FLOW Z-PINCH (COMPACT PULSED POWER)
breakthroughs: stable pinches at fusion conditions
electrodes that survive millions of pulses
studies.note: A current through a plasma column squeezes it; sheared flow keeps it stable. Compact, pulsed, and still a long way from net power.

studies.name: TOKAMAK OR STELLARATOR POWER BASE
breakthroughs: a plant that sends more power to the grid than it uses
materials that survive the neutrons
studies.note: Far too heavy to fly. On the ground or the Moon it is cheap power that pays for launches (more budget in the game).

studies.name: INERTIAL FUSION PULSE PROPULSION
breakthroughs: lasers efficient enough to fly
firing many capsules a second for years
studies.note: Lasers crush fuel capsules; in 2022 a lab got more fusion energy out than the lasers delivered, but far less than the lasers drew from the wall.
